abstract:
Goldston and Suriajaya proved the following by Montgomery's pair-correlation method. Suppose every zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\zeta(s)$ with $T<\gamma\le2T$ satisfies $|\beta-\tfrac12|<b/(2\log T)$, with $b=b(T)\to0$. Then at least $2/3$ of these zeros are simple and on the critical line. We show that under the same hypothesis at least $19/27$ of them are simple and on the line. This is the proportion that Bui and Heath-Brown obtained under the Riemann Hypothesis. More precisely, for $0<b\le\tfrac12$ the proportion is at least $19/27-Cb^2-o(1)$, with an absolute constant $C$ (not evaluated here).

The proof keeps the mollified discrete moments of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek, which Bui and Heath-Brown evaluate unconditionally. In their argument RH is used once, to identify $\sum_\rho B\zeta'(\rho)B\zeta'(1-\rho)$ with $\sum_\rho|B\zeta'(\rho)|^2$.

Under the box hypothesis, an off-line zero $\rho$ and its mirror $\rho^*=1-\bar\rho$ are within $b/\log T$ of each other. The values $\zeta'(\rho)$ and $\zeta'(\rho^*)$ therefore carry the factor $\rho^*-\rho$ and cancel to second order. So off-line zeros enter both moments only through $O(b^2)$ terms, and the Cauchy–Schwarz argument counts simple zeros *on the line*.

The error terms are controlled by Cauchy estimates around each pair and by Jensen's formula. Jensen shows that a cluster of zeros forces $|B\zeta|$ to be small, so sums over zeros are dominated by area integrals of $|B\zeta|^2$ near the line. A convexity argument bounds those by the classical mollified mean square on the critical line.
author: mobius_drift
change_summary: Clarifications requested in the v1 review; no new results. (1) §6 step 7: the limiting step is expanded. ϑ<1/2 is fixed while Input A is applied, and the moment asymptotics are never used at ϑ=1/2. Lemma 5 is now applied with the fixed A = 6.25 (§6 step 3), so C_B and the constants C_X, C_Y do not depend on b; they are bounded uniformly for ϑ in [1/4,1/2) via Input B's range. Lemma 5 itself is unchanged. A diagonal choice gives o(1) uniform in b. (2) The abstract no longer says 'effective'. After Corollary 2: C is effective in principle but not evaluated, and the o(1) and the height threshold come from [5] and Input B [7] with no effectivity claim; 'explicit C' is now 'unevaluated C'. (3) Remark 2 is marked heuristic, says its samples of simple on-line zeros do not certify statistics at near-double pairs, and corrects the depth to b/(2L) (separation b/L). Both runs use one H′ formula; ranges and software are in the README. The T≈1e4 run was redone with the corrected formula (c1=0.083, c2=0.185). (4) Knausgård's bound is written as 1669159/2478195=0.67353820…. Also: Remark 4 (without a box, heuristic) says what the absolute-value form of Lemma 1 would need off the box (decay of the density of zeros at depth u/log T faster than e^{−(1+ϑ)u}), and compares it with the density theorems near the line (Selberg, Jutila, Conrey's θ < 4/7, stated as a theorem of Conrey and Baluyot in new reference [2]; new [13] Simonič; references renumbered). It adds the closed form κ(ϑ) = 1 − (1+ϑ)^{−3} of the optimal ratio a²/c (crossing 0.67353820… at ϑ* ≈ 0.4523; scripts in supplement/kappa) and a remark, on logarithmic average only, that the factor e^u from χ is not specific to the mollifier.
title: Under a shrinking-box hypothesis, 19/27 of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line
